output.summary: A large deciduous tree endemic to tropical and subtropical eastern Australia. When leafless, it can be covered in bright scarlet, bell-shaped flowers; its pods contain yellow seeds surrounded by hairs that irritate on contact. Indigenous Australians ate Brachychiton seeds raw or roasted after removing these hairs, and also ate young-tree roots.
